feed.description: Investing conversations for normal humans: frameworks, risk, and the habits that matter more than predictions.
feed.title: Long Horizon Notes

bullets: Leverage feels free until the day it isn't — an insight from a 2016 economist talk that still holds up as a warning about hidden financing risk.
Most investment blow-ups stem from fine bets financed the wrong way rather than from bad bets — the failure lies in the borrowing, not the underlying asset.
An index fund owned outright is patient, able to ride out downturns; the same fund on margin can be forced to sell at the worst possible moment.
Risk sits in the borrowing against an asset rather than in the asset itself — identical holdings carry very different danger depending on how they are financed.
